mcqs.question: Arrange the metals Na, Ca, Mg, and Fe in order of decreasing reactivity with water at room temperature.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metal sodium reacts vigorously with cold water, calcium reacts moderately, magnesium reacts only with hot water, and iron shows negligible reaction. Hence the decreasing order is Na > Ca > Mg > Fe.

mcqs.question: Which metal among the following does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from acids. Zinc, iron and magnesium are above hydrogen and do react, liberating H₂.

mcqs.question: In the reaction of a metal with an acid, hydrogen gas is liberated. Which statement correctly describes this hydrogen displacement process?

options.A: The metal is oxidized and hydrogen ions are reduced to hydrogen gas.
options.B: The metal is reduced and hydrogen ions are oxidized to water.
options.C: Both metal and hydrogen ions remain unchanged.
options.D: The metal acts as a catalyst and is regenerated at the end.

mcqs.answer: The metal is oxidized and hydrogen ions are reduced to hydrogen gas.
mcqs.explanation: When a reactive metal contacts an acid, the metal loses electrons (oxidation) and the hydrogen ions (H⁺) gain electrons (reduction) to form H₂ gas. This is the classic displacement reaction.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: According to the reactivity series, which metal can displace zinc from its aqueous solution?
mcqs.explanation: Iron lies above zinc in the reactivity series, so iron ions can be reduced while zinc metal is oxidized, causing zinc to go into solution. Copper, lead and silver are below zinc and cannot displace it.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best distinguishes the reaction of alkali metals with water from that of transition metals with water?

options.A: Alkali metals react vigorously producing H₂ and a strong base, while most transition metals show little or no reaction.
options.B: Both alkali and transition metals react similarly, producing only metal hydroxides.
options.C: Transition metals react more vigorously than alkali metals, producing explosive hydrogen.
options.D: Alkali metals do not react with water, whereas transition metals do.

mcqs.answer: Alkali metals react vigorously producing H₂ and a strong base, while most transition metals show little or no reaction.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals (e.g., Na, K) react rapidly with water, forming hydroxides and liberating hydrogen gas. Most transition metals (e.g., Fe, Cu) are either unreactive or react only with hot water/steam, showing a clear distinction.

mcqs.question: A metal X reacts with dilute H₂SO₄ to evolve hydrogen gas. Which metal could X be?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium is above hydrogen in the reactivity series and reacts with dilute acids, producing MgSO₄ and H₂. Copper, silver and gold are below hydrogen and do not evolve hydrogen with dilute acids.

mcqs.question: When zinc metal is added to dilute hydrochloric acid, hydrogen gas is evolved. Which concept does this illustrate?

options.A: Hydrogen displacement where zinc is higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series.
options.B: Formation of a covalent bond between zinc and hydrogen.
options.C: Oxidation of hydrogen and reduction of zinc.
options.D: No reaction occurs because zinc is inert.

mcqs.answer: Hydrogen displacement where zinc is higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc, being above hydrogen in the reactivity series, displaces hydrogen ions from HCl, reducing them to H₂ gas while zinc itself is oxidized to Zn²⁺. This is a classic hydrogen displacement reaction.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: A student places a strip of iron in a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Predict the observation based on the reactivity series.

options.A: Iron dissolves and copper metal deposits, because iron is more reactive than copper.
options.B: No reaction occurs because copper is more reactive than iron.
options.C: Iron and copper exchange electrons but no visible change.
options.D: Copper dissolves and iron deposits, because copper is more reactive.

mcqs.answer: Iron dissolves and copper metal deposits, because iron is more reactive than copper.
mcqs.explanation: Iron is above copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions from CuSO₄. Iron oxidizes to Fe²⁺, and copper ions are reduced to metallic copper, which appears as a reddish deposit.
